home.journalSummary: Quiet essays on textile care, architectural drapery proportions, and living alongside natural fibers.

journalPosts.title: The Art of Hanging Floor-to-Ceiling Linen Drapery
journalPosts.excerpt: How ceiling-mounted tracks, double fullness, and translucent Belgian flax soften proportions and sculpt shifting daylight.
journalPosts.body: Architectural drapery does more than frame a window—it alters the acoustics, vertical scale, and emotional temperature of an entire room. At LOOMÉ, we recommend mounting discreet recessed tracks flush with the ceiling line and specifying at least 2.2x fabric fullness so unbleached flax falls in calm, uninterrupted columns. Allow a gentle 1.5 cm kiss at the floor for tailored minimalism, or a 6 cm break for classic European romance.

journalPosts.title: Why Normandy Flax Grows More Luminous With Every Wash
journalPosts.excerpt: Inside the slow dew-retting harvest that gives European linen its hollow, breathable fiber structure and effortless drape.
journalPosts.body: Unlike mass-produced textiles treated with chemical softeners that fade after three washes, true long-staple Normandy flax relies on coastal rain and morning dew to naturally separate fibers from the stem. Each time you launder stonewashed linen in cool water and line-dry in dappled shade, natural pectins relax further—creating a matte, supple luster that endures for generations.

journalPosts.title: Layering Ivory, Sage Olive & Champagne in Calm Rooms
journalPosts.excerpt: A tactile guide to balancing matte bouclé, washed velvet, and raw linen without visual clutter.
journalPosts.body: Monochrome interiors sing when contrast comes from weave structure rather than loud pattern. Pair a crisp 165 GSM sheer linen against heavy herringbone upholstery, then introduce a single muted sage olive velvet cushion and champagne merino throw to anchor the seating group. As afternoon sun shifts across plaster walls, each fiber reflects light at a subtly different cadence.

about.heading: Woven with Quiet Reverence for Material & Light
about.body: Founded as an editorial textile maison, LOOMÉ partners with family-owned weaving mills across Belgium, Northern Italy, and Portugal. We create architectural drapery, tactile bedding, and heirloom fabrics designed to bring calm, warmth, and enduring beauty to everyday living.
about.collageDescription: From raw Normandy flax stalks to final steam-pressed drapery panels, every stage honors slow craft.
about.history: We reject disposable decor in favor of honest natural fibers that deepen in character with time. Each palette is formulated to harmonize effortlessly with travertine, oak, plaster, and shifting natural daylight.
